Approved findings

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

Training a Helpful and Harmless Assistant with Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (2204.05862v1) · paper method: For RLHF training, the paper combines 137k prompts from the static human-feedback dataset with 369k model-generated prompts; the synthetic prompts are distinct from the human comparison labels used to train preference models.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

Training a Helpful and Harmless Assistant with Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (2204.05862v1) · paper method: A controlled 52B helpfulness experiment uses equal-sized data and identical hyperparameters and finds that a base/rejection-sampling/online mixture is preferred by crowdworkers to all-base data.

cohort3.claim.helpful.online-controlled-comparison

  • This assertion originated as an author proposal; separate review receipts determine its current status.
  • Version-specific author-reported study; experiments, raw dataset records and formal proofs were not independently reproduced or verified.
  • In this paper, online iterations retrain new models rather than continually updating one model. This is not a guarantee of worst-case safety.
  • Training a Helpful and Harmless Assistant with Reinforcement Learning from Human FeedbackLocator: Physical PDF pp20-22, section4.5 and Figure16; excerpt at physical p22, pdftotext-layout line 16 (1-based).

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

Training a Helpful and Harmless Assistant with Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (2204.05862v1) · paper method: The study collects helpfulness dialogues by choosing the more helpful response and red-team dialogues by choosing the more harmful response; retained comparisons are treated as equally weighted binary labels without ties.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

Training a Helpful and Harmless Assistant with Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (2204.05862v1) · paper method: Workers are recruited through US MTurk and Upwork; the authors select workers using writing/dialogue spot checks rather than agreement-based label filtering, and explicitly note that the worker distribution changes over the project.
